item.title: US Interior Sec. Burgum on Trump Dividend, Gas Prices and Data Centers
item.description: US Interior Secretary Doug Burgum says Congress should approve President Donald Trump's $5,000 payment for Americans. Burgum says "everything's on the table" when it comes to trying to lower gas prices. The secretary also says data centers could benefit neighborhoods. He speaks to Kailey Leinz on "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Republican Midterm Convention 2026 Live Updates: Trump, Vance Speak in Dallas
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Future of US Sports Investment
item.description: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily is live from Power Players in New York City, a sports-focused event hosted by Bloomberg's own Vanessa Perdomo-Maglione and Randall Williams. Gotham FC lead Owner and Governor Carolyn Tisch Blodgett discusses how the sports investment landscape has evolved. Plus, 'The Deal' Podcast co-host Jason Kelly talks about the rising popularity of tennis and attention on the US Open. Finally, Bloomberg Managing Editor of Media & Entertainment Lucas Shaw discusses how steaming channels like Amazon and Apple are reshaping their sports strategy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump’s $5,000 Payout Promise Would Be a Waste
item.description: Not only does President Trump not have the money to give every American adult $5,000, but there's a much better financial solution that could bring the cost of living down for everyone, Bloomberg Opinion Executive Editor Robert Burgess says. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Democrats Tap Trump’s Economic Playbook at Republican Midterm Convention
item.description: Party leaders plan to keep hammering the president on the cost of living.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Trump’s Surgeon General Pick Invested in Tobacco, McDonald’s
item.description: President Donald Trump’s nominee for surgeon general reported investments in companies including McDonald’s Corp., Monster Beverage Corp., Coca-Cola Co. and the tobacco company Philip Morris International Inc., according to her financial disclosures made public Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Cohrs Zhang and Bill Allison

item.title: Fetterman’s Split With Democrats Deepens Over Video Boosting GOP
item.description: For months, Democrats in Pennsylvania have watched Senator John Fetterman appear to drift further from the party that elected him. His appearance at the Republican convention in Texas this week was a breaking point for some.
item.dc:creator: Liz Skalka

item.title: UAE to Invest $46 Billion in Germany
item.description: UAE Minister of State for Foreign Trade Thani Bin Ahmed Al Zeyoudi says that €10 billion of the €40 billion the UAE is investing in Germany will go to Bavaria, and the rest will be for a variety of sectors, including AI. Speaking exclusively with Bloomberg's Abeer Abu Omar, he says that the Emirates is working toward gaining direct access to Berlin, which he hopes will be finalized before the end of the year. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Headlines Texas Convention
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz is live in Dallas. On today's show, Republican Congressman Jim Jordan of Ohio, former Texas Congressman Beto O'Rourke, former US Ambassador to Japan Rahm Emanuel and Republican Congressman Beth Van Duyne of Texas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Politicians Grapple With Higher Rates Ahead Of Midterms
item.description: Bloomberg's Josh Wingrove joins Scarlet Fu on "Bloomberg Deals." Facing waning popularity and depleted enthusiasm, President Trump offered voters a quid pro quo: elect Republicans and get a $5,000 payout. This comes as US public debt recently surpassed $40 trillion for the first time. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Data Center Construction Should Be Decided At 'Local Level' Says Beth Van Duyne
item.description: Republican Representative from Texas Beth Van Duyne said that decisions around data center construction should be made at the local level and that local governments and constituents should have conversations about the reality of the impact on the ground, but that she does not see it as a federal issue. The Congresswoman also discussed the midterm races in Texas and said that she expects more PAC money to flow into statewide races. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jim Jordan Sidesteps Trump Payout Support, Wants to See Proposal
item.description: Republican Representative from Ohio Jim Jordan stopped short of supporting President Trump's pledge to give all adult Americans $5,000 if the Republicans win the midterm election and said that he would want to 'see the proposal.' The Congressman also discussed his priorities for the midterm election, saying that he is focused on helping Republican candidates across the country win their races, including embattled Ohio congressman Max Miller. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Yields Surge, Calling Bessent's Bluff | Real Yield 9/10/2026
item.description: "Bloomberg Real Yield" highlights the market-moving news you need to know. Today's guests: Janus Henderson Head of Multi-Asset Macro Investing Mike Contopoulus, JPMorgan Asset Management US CIO of US GFICC Kay Herr, Capital Group Fixed Income Asset Class Lead Margaret Steinbach, and CreditSights Head of IG & Macro Strategy Zachary Griffiths. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Is OPEC Losing Its Clout?
item.description: OPEC’s grip on the global oil market is weakening. With the UAE already out and Venezuela mulling its options, Saudi Arabia’s influence is being diluted, shifting more oil-market power to the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rahm Emanuel Says Bessent's Rhetoric Overshoots His Actions
item.description: Rahm Emanuel, who served as Ambassador to Japan under President Obama, said that Scott Bessent's rhetoric around the economy and the US backing of the Japanese Yen is 'harder than his action' and 'overshoots' his capacity to deliver. Emanuel also discussed the midterm elections and said that the American people will see through Trump's $5,000 dividend 'gimmick.' (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Canada Targets Millions of Drones, With a Third for Ukraine
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy signed a declaration of a 100-year partnership between their two countries, as Canada pledged to boost its drone production capacity and send one-third to Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Nojoud Al Mallees, Iain Boekhoff and Aliaksandr Kudrytski

item.title: Scrutiny of Sánchez Grows With Release of Ceuta Papers
item.description: Pedro Sánchez had hoped to draw a line under his government’s handling of the migration crisis in Ceuta by declassifying documents late last night. Instead, it’s had the opposite effect.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Basteiro

item.title: Trump Promises $500 Back for Obamacare Plans Republicans Cut
item.description: The Trump administration pledged to send $500 each to nearly 1 million Americans it said paid too much for federally backed Obamacare health insurance, whose funding was at the center of a political standoff that led to last year’s record-long government shutdown.
item.dc:creator: Ike Swetlitz and Melos Ambaye

item.title: US Supreme Court Blocks Missouri GOP-Backed Voting Map Again
item.description: The US Supreme Court blocked Missouri from using a congressional map engineered by GOP lawmakers in the midterm elections, appearing to resolve a multifaceted legal fight that had cast uncertainty over how districts will be drawn for the November vote.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg

item.title: Algeria Cuts Diplomatic Ties With UAE, Citing ‘Hostile’ Acts
item.description: Algeria said it decided to sever diplomatic relations with the United Arab Emirates after exhausting “all available avenues” for maintaining ties.
item.dc:creator: Salah Slimani and Tarek El-Tablawy
